IO1_direct_inputs.name: consent_request
IO1_direct_inputs.source: Feature requires consent (messaging, location sharing, sensor access, etc)

IO2_direct_outputs.name: consent_audit_log
IO2_direct_outputs.schema_ref: { user_id, feature, action, timestamp, method, ip_address?, device_id? }

IO3_transformations.operation: Check if user has valid consent
IO3_transformations.algorithm: Query user_consents table. Check if granted_at exists and revoked_at is null.
INSERT user_consents record with timestamp, method. Log to audit trail.
UPDATE user_consents set revoked_at. Cascade to feature (stop location sharing, stop sensor access).

DW1_upstream_pipeline.description: User or system requests access to feature (messaging, location, sensors)

DW2_downstream_pipeline.description: Check if user has granted consent
If no consent: show consent modal. If consent: allow feature.
If user grants: record in user_consents table and audit log
If user revokes consent: feature immediately stops (location sharing disabled, sensors stopped)

P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Consent check on every feature access (should be <100ms). Consent revocation cascade (may take several seconds). Audit logging at scale (real-time writes).
P.P2_defensibility: Explicit consent for each feature. Granular control (per-sensor, per-feature). Audit trail for transparency. Easy revocation (no friction).
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence. Simple consent tracking. Well-established pattern.
P4_failure_modes: Consent check fails → feature blocked even though consent granted (mitigate: default to 'allowed' after first verification)
Revocation not propagated → feature continues after revoke (mitigate: explicit stop signal, periodic re-check)
Audit logging fails → no legal record (mitigate: async audit, never block consent for audit failure)
User forgets they granted consent → privacy concern (mitigate: consent management page shows all active consents)
P.P5_backup_plan: If consent check fails: allow feature (trust local cache). If revocation fails: escalate to manual intervention. If audit fails: async retry.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate consent check failure. Test revocation cascade on all features. Test audit logging failure. Test concurrent grant/revoke.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for consent check logic. Integration tests for grant/revoke. Load tests for concurrent consent operations (1000/s). End-to-end tests for full consent flow. Cascade tests (revoke one feature, verify others unaffected). Audit accuracy tests.
P.P8_benchmarks: Consent check: <100ms. Grant consent: <200ms. Revoke consent: <500ms (including cascade). Audit logging: <500ms (async). Revocation accuracy: 100% (feature stops immediately). Audit coverage: 100%.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial CONFolder for consent manager module

L.L1_legal_considerations: GDPR requires explicit, informed, granular consent. CCPA grants right to opt-out. User must be able to revoke easily. Consent method documented (scroll, tap, e-sign). Audit trail proves consent was given.
L.L3_consent_requirements: Per-feature or per-sensor granularity required. User must see clear description of what's being consented to. Consent method recorded. Ability to revoke at any time.
L.L4_liability_notes: Consent is legal evidence of user authorization. Improper consent is regulatory violation. Auditing consent changes is critical for defense. Revocation must be immediate and complete.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Consent storage: ~100B per consent per user. Audit logging: ~500B per event. At 10k users with 10 consents each, 1k events/day: ~100KB/day storage. Negligible cost.
F.F3_revenue_impact: User trust increases with clear consent management (positive impact). Regulatory compliance enables operation (required, not optional).

S.S1_cybersecurity: Consent records stored plaintext (low sensitivity, not credentials). Audit log written securely. Consent revocation immediate (no delay). Rate limiting on consent changes (prevent spam).
S.S2_data_privacy: User sees own consent list. Admin sees only consent status (not audit details unless needed). Revocation is right-to-delete trigger (data stops being collected immediately).
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Audit log encrypted in transit (TLS). Audit log may be encrypted at rest (not strictly required, but good practice).
S.S4_access_control: User sees and controls own consent. Admin sees consent status for support/debugging. Legal can access audit log for compliance.
S.S5_audit_requirements: Complete audit log of all consent grants/revokes: who, when, method, outcome. Audit trail retention: 7 years (legal requirement).

X.X1_notes: Consent manager is critical for GDPR/CCPA compliance and user trust. Granular consent (per-sensor, per-feature) gives users control. Audit trail proves compliance. Revocation cascade ensures respected user wishes. Integration with all features (messaging, location, sensors) is essential.
X2_open_questions: Consent granularity: per-feature or per-sensor? (per-sensor is more granular but more complex)
Default state: opt-in or opt-out? (opt-in = safer, opt-out = higher adoption)
Consent method: scroll to accept, or explicit checkbox? (scroll has UX issues, checkbox clearer)
X.X3_related_research: GDPR consent requirements. CCPA opt-out mechanisms. Consent management platforms. Legal audit trail requirements. Privacy-by-design principles.
